messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@finovate.ai>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@finovate.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity alignment: reserved GPU evaluation — post-call summary

Hi Janelle / Ben — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please correct anything I missed.

High-level pain points you emphasized:
- Cost volatility during unpredictable nightly spikes (current infra bills up 3x on peak days).
- Need for stronger isolation for regulated workloads (HIPAA-equivalent & customer contractual language).
- Long cold-start regeneration of KV cache after node recycling; affects p95/p99 tails.

Current stack (what you described):
- On-prem Kubernetes (GKE private) running Triton + custom microservices for request routing.
- Models hosted internally with local caching layer backed by Redis; cache not persisted across restarts.
- Traffic: baseline ~6 TPS, daily peak bursts up to ~18 TPS (10–30 minute spikes), nightly batch inference runs at low priority.

Success criteria you gave for a Dedicated pilot:
1) Predictable committed throughput: stable p95 latency target <= 120ms for typical prompts at baseline TPS.
2) Cost predictability: predictable monthly committed spend with clear burst pricing for short spikes.
3) Data isolation & controls: private networking, KMS integration, and audit logs for model inputs.
4) Failure modes: fallbacks and graceful degradation (auto-fallback to smaller model variant if capacity constrained).

Operational constraints & autoscaling/burst preferences:
- Prefer reserved pool for baseline capacity (you suggested 4–8 GPUs initially).
- Burst policy: allow 2x short-duration burst for traffic spikes (10–30 minutes) with automatic graceful throttling if sustained beyond burst window.
- Warm KV cache persistence across preemptible restarts is important.

What Redwood will provide next (action items):
1) Sean / Eng team: share a preliminary Dedicated worksheet with cost and performance scenarios (attached: redwood-dedicated-worksheet.xlsx).
2) You: share a 48-hour sample of production telemetry and a CSV of representative request sizes (attached: distro-inference-sample-metrics.csv).
3) Schedule a 90-minute technical deep-dive with our infra + runtime engineers to validate kernel/quantization trade-offs and KV cache persistence approach.
4) Draft a 6-month pilot SOW + pilot SLA for your legal/procurement review; include burst pricing and rollback policy.

Proposed tentative timings:
- We’ll review telemetry by Wed 3/18 (you confirm).
- Technical deep-dive target: week of 3/22 (Monica to coordinate availability).
- Pilot SOW draft: by 3/20 for your initial review.

Attachments referenced: redwood-dedicated-worksheet.xlsx, distro-inference-sample-metrics.csv.

Thanks — Sean

Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@finovate.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@finovate.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity alignment: reserved GPU evaluation — post-call summary

Thanks Sean — this is a solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- On cost volatility: our billing spikes are often driven by 15–25 minute promotional campaigns and occasional QA regressions (bad prompts). We want the committed model to cover normal traffic and have explicit, capped burst pricing.
- On isolation: we cannot share customer-identifiable inputs outside our VPC. The private deployment flow + KMS is mandatory for the pilot.
- Cache: Redis persistence is something we’re evaluating; long-term we want an approach that preserves KV cache or can warm it fast on node replacement.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Can reserved pools be pinned to a specific tenant/account so we get strict isolation?
2) During bursts, what priority is given to reserved vs shared traffic, and what are SLO guarantees for burst windows?
3) Any limitations on model size for the reserved pool approach (e.g., >28B models requiring special instance types)?

I attached our traffic extract (finovate-current-traffic-avg-peak.pdf) — it includes a 7-day sample and notes on payload size.

If these constraints are addressable, we’re keen to move to a pilot as discussed. Suggested deep-dive attendees from our side: our infra lead Ben, and our ML platform lead (TBD).

—Janelle
Janelle Park
Head of Platform Engineering | Finovate AI
janelle.park@finovate.ai

Sean / Karthik — quick internal note after Janelle’s clarifications.

Proposed approach (internal draft):
- Offer a 6-month pilot: baseline 4 x A100-equiv reserved, with a burst bucket allowing up to 2x for 30 minutes per day before capped overage applies.
- Include private deployment option (VPC peering) and customer-managed KMS.
- Ensure we run a warm-up job during node bring-up to pre-populate KV cache from their persisted snapshot (Diego to validate feasibility with runtime team).
- We’ll prepare a sensitivity table: cost @ baseline (4 GPUs), cost @ steady-state (8 GPUs), and cost during 2x burst for 30m/day. Monica to assemble by 3/18.

Assigning owners:
- Monica: pilot commercial worksheet + cost sensitivity
- Diego: runtime validation on cache persistence / warm-start approach
- Karthik: SLA & legal escalation path (priority routing, fallback policies)

I’ll schedule the deep-dive once we confirm attendees from Finovate.
